original_text:
I have been reading about multi statement and multi table transactions. Currently delta only supports ACID at single table level and single transaction only. 

In order to handle multi table and multi transactions; There is going to be a shift from file system managed delta log(s3 or adls) to Catalog Managed logs in the future versions of delta lake. 

I think this is similar to how iceberg already operate ( not an expert in iceberg). In iceberg;catalog is already a final source of truth. 
 
As we all know Delta Lake stored all table metadata in the _delta_log directory:

1) Every commit is a JSON log entry.
2) When new parquet files are added; and 
once it logs the entry in transaction log; it consider it as a commit.

Here all powers reside within file system. What catalog can do is sync the metadata from transaction logs.

In the future versions of delta lake; we’ll see catalog getting more powers. Instead of the file system being the source of truth; catalog will have powers to accept or reject the transaction.

This is very helpful if multiple people are working on same table and they want to read their own versions of the data until you commit the transaction. 

Or if same person is working on multiple tables and wants to commit all the tables. Either the commits on the tables pass or all fail. In the current system, where delta logs are stored in S3, once the json entry for one table is logged, even if the other table fail, you can’t do anything about it and can’t rollback.

However, now catalog will decide whether the commit that was done in delta log; is it a valid commit or not. If it’s not valid ; it’ll just ignore that json file and vaccum will just delete that json log. 

If you are more interested to know about details; you can read more about how classic databases deal with repeatable reads, read your own writes etc.
